 Rocket League Connects NFL Quarterbacks and South African Esports

 Rocket League is attracting attention from professional American football players and aspiring esports competitors, with New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye associated with late-night tournaments and South African high school teams pursuing competitive success. Reports published October 19 and 20, 2026, highlighted the game's appeal across different levels of competition, from an NFL player's gaming routine to a school team's championship achievements in Cape Town.
 According to a report published by Barstool Sports on October 20, Maye previously played Rocket League tournaments every night until 1 a.m. Since getting married, he has shifted to tournaments scheduled for 8 p.m. The report described his gaming habits as an unexpected connection between professional football and competitive video gaming.

 Rocket League combines soccer-style competition with vehicles, requiring players to control cars while maneuvering a ball toward opponents' goals. Its competitive format has also become a platform for young players in South Africa, where school-based teams are developing skills through organized tournaments.

 Seth Solomons, a high school player representing the CDV Wolves Prime esports team at Curro Durbanville High School in Cape Town, has spent years developing his Rocket League skills. The three-player team won consecutive high school championships in 2025 and 2026, according to Eyewitness News.
 "I play Rocket League. I've been a gamer for 6 years now. I've put up about 1000 hours to prepare a year of training for competitions." Seth Solomons told Eyewitness News.
 Solomons said his experience reflects the preparation required for competitive gaming. His family and friends became more supportive after seeing the team's abilities, and he hopes to compete internationally and establish a long-term career in gaming.

 Tanya Neethling, esports manager at Curro Durbanville High School, oversees the CDV Wolves' competitive program and described the team's defense of its title.
 "I'm Tanya Neethling and I'm representing the CDV Wolves from Curro Durbanville High School in Cape Town," Tanya Neethling told Eyewitness News. "We won Rocket League last year..So this year they qualified again and we've back to defend our title. There are three players."
 Neethling said the wider school community supports the players, although she believes esports still faces skepticism from people who do not consider competitive gaming a sport.
 Also Read

 "Oh, I think there's a misperception about esports in general. A lot of people still don't perceive esports as an actual sport," said Tanya Neethling to Eyewitness News. "So that's the fight we have: is that people, schools, and companies need to recognise esports as an actual sport because the teams they win awards, they compete at such a high skill and I just want people to change their mindset and to see that esports is not only sitting and playing a game for a lot of players it's way more than a game they play competitively."
 Neethling also highlighted esports as an inclusive competitive environment where women, children and people with disabilities can participate online. She argued that recognition from schools and businesses could help players gain greater acceptance for their achievements.
 Johann von Backstrom, senior manager for content and gaming at Telkom, pointed to school programs as a way to strengthen the wider competitive gaming ecosystem and identify emerging talent.

 "Developing at the grassroots level is elevating the gameplay for the bigger teams and giving them a lot of new talent that's coming through in the pipeline," said Johann von Backstrom to Eyewitness News.
 Von Backstrom also said girls account for nearly half of tournament players and noted that accessible mobile gaming can make participation easier for young people across Africa. The school-level development of players such as Solomons is part of a broader effort to expand competitive gaming opportunities beyond established professional teams.
